domains.details: The Nucleocapsid (N) Protein is said to have a "tight" structure. The carboxyl end of the N-terminal domain possesses an RNA binding domain. Sequence alignments show 2 regions of reasonable conservation, approx. 64-103 and 201-329 [[cite:PUB00003173]]. A whole functional protein is required for encapsidation to take place [[cite:PUB00005627]].

Members of the Mononegavirales including the Paramyxoviridae, like other non-segmented negative strand RNA viruses, have an RNA-dependent RNA polymerase composed of two subunits, a large protein L and a phosphoprotein P. This is a protein family of the L protein. The L protein confers the RNA polymerase activity on the complex. The P protein acts as a transcription factor [[cite:PUB00000746]].

This V domain of L RNA-polymerase carries a new motif, GxxTx(n)HR, that is essential for mRNA cap formation. Nonsegmented negative-sense (NNS) RNA viruses, Mononegavirales, cap their mRNA by an unconventional mechanism. Specifically, 5'-monophosphate mRNA is transferred to GDP derived from GTP through a reaction that involves a covalent intermediate between the large polymerase protein L and mRNA. The V region is essential for this process [[cite:PUB00061985]].
